alex_support: Ticket TL-4412 — Admin console shows 'Credit applied' toast but ledger has no entry. Happening intermittently (~15% of manual grant attempts). Repro steps below, attaching curl/response we captured.

maria_ops: Can you confirm this is only manual grants from the support console and not promo code flows?

alex_support: Only manual grants so far (support console). Affects 3 customers across regions. Quick repro: 1) Support console -> Customer -> Credits -> Grant 2) Submit 1000 units 3) See success toast immediately 4) Check ledger -> no row.

alex_support: Repro curl/logs:
```bash
curl -X POST https://backoffice.internal/v1/grants \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer *****" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: grant-req-20240301-abc" \
  -d '{"user_id":"cust_9x","amount":1000,"reason":"trial"}'
# -> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
# {"error":"rate_limited","message":"please retry"}
# headers: X-Request-ID: req_abc123, x-backoffice-node: b-3, Retry-After: <missing>
```

tim_backend: I pulled grants-service logs for that window. We're emitting 429s from the concurrency limiter (token-bucket) when db write latency spikes. Console client retries every ~200ms with no jitter which amplifies the pressure.

jenna_billing: Important: do NOT reapply credits for affected customers until we confirm ledger state and idempotency. We already have one billing complaint about mismatched balances.

deploy-bot: grants-service v2.4.1 deployed by tim_backend at 1872001200

daniel_prod: Looking at the backoffice code path — when ledger write times out we sometimes return a 200 to the UI because the grant RPC returns before ledger finalization. UI treats that as success. That's wrong; UI should wait for ledger ack or we should return 202/pending.

alex_support: Paste of a representative log segment:
"2024-11-02T15:12:02Z req=req_abc123 grants: attempting ledger insert -> timeout, ack=false"
"2024-11-02T15:12:02Z req=req_abc123 grants: returning status=200 to console (grant accepted)"
"2024-11-02T15:12:02Z req=req_abc123 ledger: async retry queued"

maria_ops: Filed UI bug RD-1023: Support console shows success toast before ledger confirm. Also created INC-7789 for the production incident.

tim_backend: Proposed mitigations: 1) Server: start returning 429 with Retry-After header when limiter hits (currently 429 body only) 2) Client: change console retry to exponential backoff with jitter (start 500ms) and honor Retry-After 3) Backoffice: make grants RPC synchronous to ledger ack for support console path or return 202 pending 4) Add stronger idempotency enforcement and logging for Idempotency-Key so we can correlate attempts. I'll push a small patch to add Retry-After and extra logging to v2.4.2.

jenna_billing: Also add a temporary mitigation: prevent the console from showing success toast for manual grants until server-side confirmation. If not possible immediately, show a 'pending' state and a link to 'check ledger'.

daniel_prod: Looks like the client retry loop is the biggest amplifier. If console keeps hammering at 200ms we will keep tripping the limiter. We should throttle client-side immediately via a config flip if needed.

alex_support: I've flagged the 3 impacted customers and paused further manual attempts. Assigning P0, cc-ing billing and ops. Will hold on reply to customers until we have a mitigation.

sre_bot: Incident created: INC-7789 — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-7789

maria_ops: Next steps: tim to push 429+Retry-After and logging; frontend team to remove optimistic success for manual grants; ops to monitor 429 rate and db write latency.

alex_support: Thanks — keep updates here.

documents.title:
devon: Heads-up — the repro-check CI for the quantized llm bring-up failed again.

eval-bot: CI job 5873 — repro-check (llama-13b-4bit) — failed

devon: We run the same seed across two runs and get different generations. Config attached below.

sara: wait, which sampling settings? temp/top_p?

devon: temp: 0.0, top_p: 0.92, seed: 12345

devon: runner config snippet:
```
sampling:
  temperature: 0.0
  top_p: 0.92
  max_new_tokens: 128
seed: 12345
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 8
quantization: 4-bit
device: cuda
```

anya: top_p + temperature=0 is weird — temp=0 should be greedy, but top_p<1 implies nucleus sampling which is stochastic. So even with temp=0 you'll sample stochastically from the top_p set.

jamal: correct. But the weird bit is that two runs with the same seed used to be identical. Something changed.

mike: I saw nondet before that came from quantized CUDA kernels (reduction ordering) — tiny FP differences can change token ranks and thus different samples for nucleus sampling.

sara: ah — so quantization + GPU nondet ordering -> different logits -> different top_p set -> different sampled token even with same RNG seed.

devon: that matches logs: per-token logits differ by 1e-5 across runs, and ranks flip at the cutoff around token 4.

anya: quick mitigation: set top_p: 1.0 (i.e., no nucleus) and use temperature: 0 to force greedy in CI. Or run with CPU deterministic kernels for the CI gate.

jamal: for CI gate I'd prefer changing the test to not require bit-exact text equality for stochastic modes. We should have two gates:
- deterministic gate (greedy / beam) -> exact match
- stochastic gate (top_p/temperature) -> metric tolerance (p95 same, distribution hash)

mike: agree. Also we should add per-request PRNG seeding inside the runtime (separate RNG per request) so we at least reproduce a specific run given the saved seed + model state.

sara: example change to runner startup (pseudo):
```
# in request handler
rng = torch.Generator(device='cuda')
rng.manual_seed(request.seed)
output = model.generate(..., generator=rng)
```

devon: we already set np.random and random, but not a device-level torch.Generator per request — good catch.

anya: longer term: add a "deterministic_sampling" flag to eval-runner that switches to deterministic tie-breaking and stable kernels (or falls back to CPU) for reproducibility runs.

jamal: logging idea — record a small artifact with: prompt hash, seed, sampling config, model checksum, quantization metadata, and the full RNG state snapshot. That will help debugging non-determinism.

mike: +1. Also add a checksum of per-layer weight dtype/order since quantization layout changes matter.

devon: CI changes proposal:
- For new-model bring-up jobs, run two modes.
  1) reproducibility mode: deterministic sampling (greedy) + device deterministic flags -> exact match
  2) stochastic evaluation: run 3 seeds, compute metric variance, fail if metric divergence > threshold
- Persist the artifact bundle for a failing run.

sara: quick implementation tasks:
- set torch.Generator per-request (devon)
- add deterministic_sampling flag & CLI/CI toggle (anya)
- change repro-check job definition to run both modes (mike)
- record artifact bundle and prompt+seed metadata (jamal)

devon: who's taking the prod/runtime note about quantized kernels potentially being non-deterministic? I'll file an infra-runtime issue if no one else.

mike: I'll open a bug with the runtime team and attach a small repro (two runs + diff of logits). I'll mark as P1 for bring-up.

eval-bot: Created issue INF-784: "Quantized CUDA inference kernels produce nondet logits affecting sampling reproducibility" — link: http://go/INF-784

jamal: CI temporary workaround: change the stock bring-up template and assert on greedy outputs only. I'll PR in 10m.

anya: small reminder — when we switch to deterministic mode in CI, make sure we don't hide real-world regressions caused by the stochastic policy (e.g., quality differences when top_p used in prod). Keep both gates.

devon: agreed. Last note: can we add a hashed signature to eval outputs (like sha256(prompt+seed+model+text)) and fail the exact-match gate only if signature mismatches? That helps correlate runs.

sara: yep that plus artifact bundle will make debugging much faster.

mike: tagging @infra-team for visibility.

devon: thanks all — will follow up with PR links and the INF-784 repro.

sara: :thumbsup:

jamal: :shipit:

mike: :eyes:

documents.title:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV2 - streaming-api-prod p99 latency breach (streaming stalls / chunking delays). Alerting on > 2s p99 for streaming endpoints. Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream. Started: 1746001123. Auto-tags: #streaming #latency #sse

ash_sre_oncall: I'm on it. Initial question: is this affecting all regions or just us-east-1?

lee_runtime_eng: I'm seeing elevated tail latency from the proxy layer in logs, looks like several connections are paused then burst. Running quick curl against SSE endpoint now.

lee_runtime_eng: curl test shows long gaps between chunks:
```
$ curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://streaming-api.prod/v1/stream?model=redwood-7b
data: {"id":"tok","text":"hello"}

(4s silence)

data: {"id":"tok","text":" world"}
```

ana_prod_support: Customer John from Acme reported slow streaming in last 10 minutes, says UI shows spinner for ~6s before any tokens appear.

marta_infra: Check envoy upstream_timeout and downstream_socket_timeout - we rolled a change to default chunk flush behavior earlier this week. I'm looking at the config now.

ash_sre_oncall: Quick triage checklist:
- confirm p95/p99 deltas (Grafana)
- check proxy (envoy) and sidecar logs for backpressure
- verify pod-level CPU/RAM and epoll wait stats
- try temporary mitigation (increase proxy chunk flush frequency / route to fallback service)

lee_runtime_eng: Grafana: p95 up from 120ms -> 380ms; p99 from 680ms -> 2.4s. Error rate unchanged. Streaming-specific endpoints have the worst tail.

lee_runtime_eng: Envoy logs: lots of "upstream response timeout" entries but responses then arrive later rather than failing. Suggests buffering on proxy side. Sample:
```
[2026-03-14T14:05:12Z] envoy upstream response timeout: stream_id=0x7f, route=/v1/stream
[2026-03-14T14:05:16Z] envoy flush: wrote 1 chunk to downstream, bytes=256
```

ash_sre_oncall: That matches client reports (long spinner then chunk). Could be chunk coalescing due to Nagle/linger or our flush threshold.

lee_runtime_eng: Quick mitigation proposal: flip the feature flag that enabled chunk_coalesce=auto, forcing immediate flush on token ready. If we can toggle that via runtime config, do it. Also bump proxy downstream_socket_timeout to 30s from 15s to avoid premature upstream timeouts while we observe.

marta_infra: I can flip the runtime flag for streaming-prod in 1 minute. Will also patch envoy config on canary pods first.

ana_prod_support: @john_cust_sre can you ask the Acme contact to capture HAR or repro steps? They mentioned Chrome only. Might be client-side buffering too.

john_cust_sre: I'll ping them; they're on a call. They say it reproduces in Chrome and Safari, so likely server side.

ash_sre_oncall: Do we risk any regressions by toggling flush? What about CPU impact?

lee_runtime_eng: Immediate flush will increase syscall frequency and slightly raise CPU usage for streamer pods, but should be safe for short mitigation. We'll monitor CPU% and p50/p95. If CPU rises >15% we rollback.

marta_infra: Runtime flag toggled on canary (streamer-3). Observing canary logs now.

lee_runtime_eng: Canary shows chunk spacing reduced to ~60ms. p99 on canary route dropped to 420ms. 

ash_sre_oncall: Rollout to 50% (blue/green) for streaming-prod. Keep alerting thresholds lowered to catch regressions.

marta_infra: Rolled to 50%. Envoy timeout bumped to 30s canary applied.

lee_runtime_eng: After 50% rollout, global p99 is down to 1.1s and counting down. UI reports from customers show tokens now arriving steadily instead of big gaps.

ana_prod_support: Acme confirms much better behavior after our changes. They still see occasional ~1s gaps but acceptable for now.

ash_sre_oncall: Good. Next steps: keep mitigations in place for 2 hours while we root cause. Logging pointers: enable detailed tcp_keepalive and flush-debug for streamer pods. Capture netstat/epoll stats.

lee_runtime_eng: Probable root causes to investigate:
- recent chunk_coalesce change that batched small writes to reduce syscalls
- envoys with differing HTTP/1.1 chunk flush semantics (we saw a config change last Wed)
- client-side TCP push buffering (socket options) interacting with Nagle/PSH timing

marta_infra: Will audit config change PRs affecting envoy and runtime-flags between 3/8 - 3/12.

ash_sre_oncall: Handoff to night oncall @ash_next at 1746002000. I'll annotate runbook and mitigation steps in the incident doc. Postmortem owner: lee_runtime_eng.

lee_runtime_eng: Noted. I'll schedule a deeper trace extraction and pair with infra to reproduce locally with high fanout.

ash_sre_oncall: Summary for customer comms: cause under investigation, immediate mitigation applied (forced flush + proxy timeout bump), visible improvement, ongoing RCA, will follow up with timeline and root cause. Ana can draft a short update to Acme.

ana_prod_support: Drafting now, ETA 10m.

marta_infra: Adding a follow-up PR to make flush defaults conservative and opt-in for coalescing.

ash_sre_oncall: Closing incident thread for active paging; keeping channel open for updates. If p99 creeps back above 2s, page SRE again. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated at 1746001790. Severity reduced to SEV3.

ash_sre_oncall: Leaving notes:
- Mitigation: runtime flag forced_flush=true, envoy downstream_socket_timeout=30s, 50% rollout then full after positive metrics
- Observed impact window: 1746001123 - 1746001790
- Postmortem: scheduled for 1746070000 (next day) with lee as owner

lee_runtime_eng: I'll attach traces and a reproducer repo before the postmortem.

john_cust_sre: Acme acknowledges fix and appreciates quick response.

ash_sre_oncall: Thanks team. If anyone sees residual issues, reply here and we'll re-open paging.

queries.query: What is the complete SOP Redwood Inference must follow to enable "customer-managed audit log export" (to the customer's cloud storage) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments-including required prerequisites, security approvals, configuration steps, validation, customer communication, and ongoing operations/ownership?

gold.goldAnswer:
1) **Intake & scoping (CS/Support)**: Open an **internal-support Jira** (Support Request; prioritize P2 standard, P1 if audit deadline <14 days), and record **customer + org_id (Hosted) / dedicated_cluster_id (Dedicated) / Private cluster**, deployment mode, regions, sink (**S3/GCS/Azure Blob**), **bucket/container + prefix + destination region**, identity method (**assume-role/IRSA/workload identity/Azure federated identity**), desired audit-log categories (**platform audit logs only-no prompt/completion logging**), retention intent, and **ops/escalation contacts + target date**; CS confirms entitlement and that export is **regional by default** (cross-region only by exception).  

2) **Prerequisites & mandatory security controls (must be satisfied before enablement)**: Treat logs as **Customer-Sensitive Metadata** and ensure **no request bodies/model outputs/token strings**; require **TLS 1.2+ in transit** and **encryption at rest** on the customer destination (S3 SSE-S3/SSE-KMS, GCS managed keys/CMEK, Azure managed keys/CMK) and encrypt any Redwood staging with Redwood KMS; enforce **least privilege** using **assume-role/workload identity only** (no long-lived customer keys stored by Redwood) scoped to **write to a specific bucket/container prefix** (and list only if required for health checks); confirm **destination ownership/allowed account** and appropriate **egress controls/allowlisting** (private endpoints preferred; for Private, customer constrains egress); align/confirm **retention** (recommend 90 days; <30 days allowed but noted; >1 year requires CS contract confirmation); ensure "**logging about logging**" is enabled (events for enable/disable, destination/auth changes, failures/retries visible in internal dashboards). Attach required evidence in the Jira: **policy/trust/binding snippet, encryption confirmation, proof of ownership IDs, and (Private) network diagram/egress statement**.  

3) **Approvals (gates)**:  
- **Gate A (CS/Support)**: request completeness + scope validation (platform audit logs only, region alignment).  
- **Gate B (Security-required for all modes)**: Security reviews encryption/least privilege/region rules and leaves a Jira comment: **"Approved for enablement"** (name/date) before production changes.  
- **Gate C (Legal/Privacy-conditional)**: required for **cross-region export**, **additional PII fields beyond standard schema**, or **bespoke contract clauses**; cross-region additionally requires **Security approval + explicit customer acknowledgement**. If controls can't be met, file a **Security exception** and link it.  

4) **Configuration & enablement (route by deployment mode)**:  
- **Hosted (Eng Platform oncall via `rdw-admin`)**: `audit-export destination upsert` (sink/region/bucket-or-container/prefix/auth-mode/role or binding) → `audit-export enable` → ensure tenant flag **`audit_export_customer_sink_enabled=true`**.  
- **Dedicated (Eng Infra)**: Decide connector placement (**Redwood-managed default** vs **dedicated-placed** exception requiring **SRE review**). Default path: update per-tenant **Terraform `dedicated-config`** `audit_export` (enabled, sink, region, destination, prefix, auth_reference) and **plan/apply**. Exception path: deploy `audit-export-connector` into the dedicated cluster (Helm), use **short-lived identity**, and configure private endpoints/egress as required.  
- **Private (Customer operator with Private Deployments guidance; bundle v2.8.0+)**: Configure `redwood-private` Helm values `auditExport.enabled=true` with sink/region/destination/prefix/format and **workload identity** (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Workload Identity) plus any private-endpoint DNS/egress settings; redeploy and restart the connector.  

5) **Validation (Redwood + customer)**: Redwood verifies connector health (**delivery_success_rate**, **delivery_lag_seconds**, **write_errors_total**) and that the tenant/cluster consumer is active; customer (coordinated by CS) confirms objects land in the agreed prefix (e.g., Hosted `org=<ORG_ID>/region=<REGION>/dt=.../hr=.../*.jsonl.gz`, Dedicated `dedicated_cluster=<ID>/region=.../...`) within ~10 minutes, and both sides spot-check one file for required fields (e.g., `event_id`, `source_service`) and **absence of inference payload fields**; remind customer delivery is **at-least-once** and they must **deduplicate by `event_id`**.  

6) **Closeout documentation & customer communication (CS owns comms)**: Update the Jira with destination identifiers, auth reference, connector placement (Dedicated), approvals, enablement timestamp, and validation evidence; CS sends/updates the customer with confirmation, expected delivery semantics/latency, and reiterates the customer owns **storage cost, retention/lifecycle, SIEM ingestion, and destination access control**.  

7) **Ongoing operations/ownership & rollback**: Redwood owns connector operation/monitoring in **Hosted/Dedicated** (and provides troubleshooting support for **Private** if customer shares logs/metrics); paging/alerting follows policy (enterprise Dedicated/Private: page on sustained failure >30 min; Hosted: alert unless multi-tenant impact). Customers should alert on **no new objects >30 min** and sustained **4xx/5xx** from storage and must notify Redwood before rotating identity/policies. If issues occur (403/trust drift, throttling, DNS/TLS/private endpoint failures), coordinate Eng + Security/CS; to stop export, **disable** (Hosted `rdw-admin audit-export disable`; Dedicated set `audit_export.enabled=false` in Terraform; Private `auditExport.enabled=false` and redeploy). If a **data-boundary/security concern** is suspected, **disable immediately** and escalate per incident process.
answerFacts: Enablement starts with CS/Support opening an internal-support Jira ticket and recording customer identity plus org_id for Hosted, dedicated_cluster_id for Dedicated, or the Private cluster identifier.

The intake ticket must capture deployment mode, regions, destination sink type (S3, GCS, or Azure Blob), bucket or container name, prefix, destination region, identity method (assume-role, IRSA, workload identity, or Azure federated identity), desired audit-log categories, retention intent, ops escalation contacts, and target date.
CS must confirm entitlement and that export is regional by default, with cross-region export only by exception.
Before enablement, Redwood must treat audit logs as Customer-Sensitive Metadata and ensure logs do not include request bodies, model outputs, or token strings.

Before enablement, data in transit must use TLS 1.2 or higher and the customer destination must have encryption at rest enabled (for example SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS on S3, managed keys or CMEK on GCS, managed keys or CMK on Azure).
Any Redwood staging involved in export must be encrypted using Redwood KMS.
Authentication must use least privilege via assume-role or workload identity only, with no long-lived customer keys stored by Redwood.
The destination permissions must be scoped to writing to a specific bucket or container prefix, with list permission only if required for health checks.
Redwood must confirm destination ownership or allowed account and required egress controls or allowlisting (private endpoints preferred; for Private deployments the customer constrains egress).
Retention expectations must be aligned during prerequisites (recommend 90 days; more than 1 year requires CS contract confirmation).
Redwood must ensure logging about logging is enabled so enable or disable actions, destination or auth changes, and failures or retries are visible in internal dashboards.

The Jira must include evidence such as the destination policy or trust or binding snippet, encryption confirmation, proof of ownership identifiers, and for Private deployments a network diagram or egress statement.
Gate A approval is CS/Support confirming request completeness and scope validation (platform audit logs only and region alignment).
Gate B approval is Security review for all deployment modes, and Security must comment Approved for enablement with name and date before production changes.

Gate C approval from Legal or Privacy is required when export is cross-region, when adding PII fields beyond the standard schema, or when bespoke contract clauses apply, and cross-region export also requires explicit customer acknowledgement.
If required controls cannot be met, a Security exception must be filed and linked in the Jira.

Hosted enablement is performed by Engineering Platform oncall using rdw-admin to upsert the audit-export destination, enable audit export, and ensure the tenant flag audit_export_customer_sink_enabled is set to true.

Dedicated enablement is performed by Engineering Infra either by updating per-tenant Terraform dedicated-config audit_export settings and applying, or by deploying an audit-export connector into the dedicated cluster as an exception that requires SRE review.

Private enablement is performed by the customer operator using Private deployment guidance (bundle v2.8.0 or later) by setting Helm values auditExport.enabled=true with sink, region, destination, prefix, format, and workload identity, then redeploying and restarting the connector.
Validation requires Redwood to verify connector health metrics including delivery_success_rate, delivery_lag_seconds, and write_errors_total and confirm the tenant or cluster consumer is active.
Validation requires the customer to confirm objects land in the agreed prefix within about 10 minutes and to spot-check a file for required fields and for absence of inference payload fields.
Customers must be told delivery is at-least-once and they must deduplicate using event_id.
Closeout requires updating the Jira with destination identifiers, auth reference, connector placement for Dedicated, approvals, enablement timestamp, and validation evidence.

Customer communication is owned by CS and must confirm enablement, expected delivery latency and semantics, and that the customer owns storage cost, retention and lifecycle, SIEM ingestion, and destination access control.
Ongoing operations ownership is Redwood monitoring and operating the connector for Hosted and Dedicated, and providing troubleshooting support for Private when the customer shares logs or metrics.
Customers should alert on no new objects for more than 30 minutes and sustained 4xx or 5xx from storage, and must notify Redwood before rotating identity or policies.
Rollback or stop procedures are: Hosted run rdw-admin audit-export disable, Dedicated set audit_export.enabled=false in Terraform, and Private set auditExport.enabled=false and redeploy.
If a data-boundary or security concern is suspected, export must be disabled immediately and escalated per the incident process.

queries.query: For an enterprise Redwood Private deployment upgrade, what is the complete go/no-go gate (required validations, required approvals, and required customer communications) mandated by Redwood's internal standards?

gold.goldAnswer:
Redwood's internal go/no-go gate for an enterprise Redwood Private production deployment upgrade requires that, at least 24h before the maintenance window, there is a change record created from the Private Upgrade Change Request template with a single named Change Owner and confirmed customer-side Change Approver and Operator contacts who will be present. The change record must document current and target versions (installer, operator/controller, runtime images, charts), the exact supported upgrade path (default N-1 to N; no unsupported major skips), and any model/runtime compatibility notes for pinned models. Rollback readiness must be demonstrated with recent backups (control-plane config state such as values/helm releases/operator CRs, any Redwood-managed PVs if present, and documentation of customer external dependencies like DB/SSO/KMS), locally available rollback artifacts (previous installer bundle, prior image tags, prior values files), a written rollback plan with commands and a time-to-rollback/time-to-restore estimate, and an explicit rollback decision point in the window plan. Preflight validations must be run and attached as evidence (standard preflight output) covering cluster capacity and node readiness, storage class/PV health, DNS and egress reachability for image pulls (or offline bundle availability where applicable), TLS/certificate status, and required Kubernetes API versions present (no deprecated APIs that will break charts). Observability readiness must be confirmed: Redwood has dashboard/alert visibility during the window (temporary access if needed) and the watch signals are available at minimum for control plane API error rate, inference 5xx, P95 latency on primary routes, and GPU utilization plus OOM/restart rates.

At window start, the Change Owner may record GO in the change record only after all required sign-offs are linked and complete: Change Management approvals per risk level (Private production upgrades are at least High), SRE SLO/error budget impact review is completed with evidence (30-day error budget remaining and explicit risk acceptance if below 25%, capacity/headroom check, monitoring watch list and alert routing to active on-call, rollback feasibility and the decision point, and confirmation of no overlapping high-risk changes), Security and Compliance sign-off is completed if triggered (auth/SSO/JWT/mTLS, RBAC/privileged accounts, TLS/cert management/trust stores, audit logging pipeline/retention/integrity, new third-party images/dependencies with digests and scan summary, or network boundary changes), and Customer Success acknowledges customer readiness and the comms plan. Final technical readiness at T=0 must be reconfirmed: preflight has no red blockers (and any yellow warnings have an owner and mitigation), there are no open Redwood-side P0/P1 incidents that would reduce ability to respond or rollback, and any change-freeze exception is approved and linked.

Customer communications must also be ready at GO time per the Planned Maintenance Comms SOP: a Customer Success-approved maintenance notice has been sent via the agreed channel with the required lead time (minimum 48h for enterprise; longer lead times may apply per risk tier), including the window in the customers timezone, expected impact, rollback posture/thresholds, required customer participation, and escalation contacts; internal heads-up has been posted at least 48h prior in #eng-oncall and #customer-success with customer name, window, change owner, link to the change record, and whether security sign-off is required (and per Private release gating, internal comms also go to #eng-releases); the window-start message is prepared to confirm backout plan and next update time; progress updates are planned at a 30-minute cadence with immediate updates for rollback or risk escalation; and an all-clear message is drafted for after the post-upgrade verification window. For Private upgrades, customer-specific maintenance is communicated directly to the customer and not posted to the public status page unless contractually required.

queries.query: Does the Hosted AWS Marketplace SKU support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK)?

gold.goldAnswer: Updated (2026 FAQ): Hosted uses provider-managed KMS keys by default, but customer-managed KMS (BYOK) is available for enterprise tenants in select regions as an add-on (subject to feasibility); if it's not available in the target region, Hosted remains provider-managed. queries.query: In a private deployment, we saw a security bug where an RBAC exclusion rule (meant to block admin/superuser access) allowed access to an admin route when a JWT omitted the entitlements claim in mid-March 2026. queries.query: What caused the savings $/day estimates in Optimization Suggestions beta to not match Arkadia Finance billing, and what UI or API changes should we make to prevent this confusion going forward?

gold.goldAnswer:
Mismatch was primarily an expectation/reconciliation gap plus an estimator input gap. The Suggestions beta $/day is an estimated compute-cost delta derived from telemetry aggregates (GPU-sec/tokens) over a trailing baseline window (typically last 7d) with an explicit stale_as_of timestamp; it is not intended to match net invoiced totals. Arkadia compared the headline $/day to Billing export total_cost net of credits/committed-use discounts and with some initial local-time vs UTC day misalignment. Realized savings were further lower because caching was only rolled out to ~50% traffic for ~12 hours (so the first 24h window would be roughly ~25% of the full-adoption daily estimate) and because cache warm-up in the first 6-12+ hours reduced hit uplift versus the estimator steady-state assumption. Additionally, for Arkadia’s Dedicated/VPC setup the estimator could not access effective contracted pricing (missing effective price feed / cost attribution gaps) and fell back to catalog/list token pricing (price_source=catalog_fallback / assumption), inflating the USD/day figure even when the percent savings remained directionally reasonable.

To prevent confusion:
UI should explicitly label $/day as "compute-cost estimate (not invoice total)" and prominently display the baseline window and stale_as_of (with timezone). Promote "assumes 100% of traffic for the shown scope" out of the Assumptions section into a top-level callout, and offer a simple rollout/adoption scaling control (or show a scaled range) for canary/A-B rollouts. When price_source is catalog_fallback or effective pricing is unavailable (especially for Dedicated/Private), de-emphasize or suppress $/day and/or show a strong warning tooltip, and consider making % savings the primary sortable field. Add a "How this matches billing" link that explains discounts/credits, invoice-only line items, and recommends comparing against Console Usage Analytics "Inference cost (compute)" for apples-to-apples.

API should surface pricing/assumption metadata needed for reconciliation: price_source (effective vs catalog_fallback/assumption), an explicit flag like savings_usd_uses_list_price, and the exact baseline window + stale_as_of used. Add an optional adoption_factor/scaled_savings field (or inputs to compute it client-side). Also downgrade/flag confidence when core pricing inputs are missing so we do not show Medium confidence while dollars are based on fallback pricing.
answerFacts: The Optimization Suggestions beta savings $/day value is an estimated compute cost delta derived from telemetry aggregates (for example GPU seconds and tokens) over a trailing baseline window (typically the last 7 days) and includes a stale_as_of timestamp.
The Optimization Suggestions beta savings $/day estimate is not intended to match net invoiced or billed totals.
Arkadia compared the headline savings $/day estimate to Billing export total_cost net of credits and committed use discounts, contributing to the mismatch.
There was an initial day boundary mismatch due to local time versus UTC alignment when comparing the estimate to billing.
Caching was only rolled out to about 50% of traffic for about 12 hours, so realized first day savings were much lower than a full adoption daily estimate.
Cache warm up during the first 6 to 12+ hours reduced cache hit uplift compared to the estimator steady state assumption, lowering realized savings versus the estimate.
For Arkadia dedicated or VPC deployments, the estimator could not access effective contracted pricing and fell back to catalog or list token pricing, inflating the USD per day estimate.
UI should label the savings $/day metric as a compute cost estimate and explicitly note it is not the invoice total.
UI should display the baseline window used for the estimate and the stale_as_of timestamp with timezone.
UI should clearly call out that the estimate assumes 100% traffic adoption for the shown scope and provide a rollout or adoption scaling control or a scaled range for partial rollouts.

When price_source is catalog_fallback or effective pricing is unavailable, UI should de emphasize or suppress the USD per day figure or show a strong warning, and consider making percent savings the primary sortable metric.

UI should include a link or explanation for how to compare to billing, including the effects of discounts and credits, and recommend comparing against compute only inference cost in usage analytics for an apples to apples view.
API should expose pricing and assumption metadata including price_source (effective versus catalog_fallback) and whether savings USD uses list price.
API should return the exact baseline window and stale_as_of values used to compute the estimate.
API should support adoption scaling via an adoption_factor and or scaled_savings field or inputs to compute scaled savings client side.
API should downgrade or flag confidence when core pricing inputs are missing so the system does not present medium confidence while dollars are based on fallback pricing.
